title: What does the NDIS Worker Screening Check require of registered providers?
description: NDIS Worker Screening Rules for registered providers: risk assessed roles, clearance exceptions, the 20 business day role list and 7 year worker records.
shortAnswer: Registered NDIS providers must assess every role, identify which are risk assessed roles, and allow only workers with an NDIS Worker Screening clearance to fill them, subject to narrow exceptions. The NDIS (Practice Standards: Worker Screening) Rules 2018 also require a written list of risk assessed roles, updated within 20 business days of a change, and a worker list kept for 7 years in a form an auditor can reconstruct day by day.
keyTakeaways: A risk assessed role is a key personnel role, a role delivering specified supports or services, or a role whose normal duties are likely to require more than incidental contact with a person with disability.
A clearance is valid for up to 5 years, is nationally recognized, and can be renewed from 90 days before expiry.
Working on application is allowed only where the state or territory permits it, with supervision by a cleared person and a written risk management plan.

Registered providers must keep a role list with five set fields, a worker list with clearance numbers and expiry dates, and copies of interim bars, suspensions and misconduct allegations, all for 7 years.
Unregistered providers are not legally required to use worker screening, although the NDIS Commission recommends it.
regulator: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, with state and territory worker screening units deciding each application
appliesTo: Registered NDIS providers and applicants for registration
Key personnel of registered providers, including directors, board members and executives
Employees, volunteers and students in risk assessed roles
Contractors and labor hire personnel placed in risk assessed roles
Sole traders who are registered providers

sections.heading: What do the NDIS worker screening rules require?

blocks.text: The rules require a registered NDIS provider to work out which of its roles carry risk, restrict those roles to people with a clearance, and keep records that prove it. The obligations sit in the [National Disability Insurance Scheme (Practice Standards: Worker Screening) Rules 2018](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2018L00887/latest/text) (the Worker Screening Rules), made under the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013. The current compilation on the Federal Register of Legislation is dated July 31, 2021. This page states the position as at November 2026.

The NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission (NDIS Commission) regulates providers against these rules. The screening decision itself is made by the worker screening unit in each state or territory, which assesses the applicant and records a 'cleared' or 'excluded' outcome in the national NDIS Worker Screening Database ([worker screening for unregistered providers](https://www.ndiscommission.gov.au/workforce/worker-screening/worker-screening-unregistered-providers)).

The rules matter for registration. Section 9 requires an applicant to be assessed by an approved quality auditor, by verification, as meeting the screening standards, and a registered provider must keep meeting them to stay registered. Part 3 of the rules (record keeping) is made under section 73Q of the Act, and the rules note that breach of that condition of registration is a civil penalty provision. Screening is a clearance decision, not training; the training that sits alongside it is covered in [what training NDIS workers need](/regulations/ndis-practice-standards-worker-training).

sections.heading: Which roles are risk assessed roles?

blocks.text: A risk assessed role is any of three things under section 5 of the Worker Screening Rules: a key personnel role; a role whose normal duties include the direct delivery of specified supports or specified services to a person with disability; or a role whose normal duties are likely to require more than incidental contact with a person with disability. The specified supports and services come from a list the NDIS Commissioner must publish under section 7.

Section 6 defines contact broadly, covering physical, face to face, oral, written and electronic communication. It says duties are likely to involve more than incidental contact if they include physically touching a person with disability, building a rapport with a person with disability as an integral and ordinary part of the duties, or having contact with multiple people with disability as part of delivering a specialist disability support or in a specialist disability accommodation setting.

The rules give two examples that the NDIS Commission repeats in its [guidance for registered providers](https://www.ndiscommission.gov.au/workforce/worker-screening/worker-screening-registered-providers). A worker who delivers mobility equipment to homes, instructs customers and adjusts the equipment is in a risk assessed role, because the contact involves openness and trust. A back office accountant who nods to customers in the lobby is not. The Commission adds that key personnel include the CEO, directors listed with ASIC, executives, managers and board members, and that people in risk assessed roles can be staff, volunteers or students on placement.

sections.heading: When can someone work in a risk assessed role without a clearance?

blocks.text: Only in the exceptions the rules list. Section 13 says a registered provider must only allow a worker to engage in a risk assessed role if the worker has a clearance. Section 14 then sets out the exceptions, and section 15 defines when a person counts as being in the process of obtaining a clearance.

items: **Working on application:** the person has submitted a complete application, is appropriately supervised by a person with a clearance, the provider is implementing a written risk management plan, and the law of the state or territory allows work while the application is pending. Section 14A switches this exception off in jurisdictions that prohibit it (often called no card, no start) unless the person has an acceptable check for that jurisdiction.
**Secondary school work experience:** a student on a formal work experience placement who is directly supervised by a worker with a clearance.

**Higher education placements:** the NDIS Commission explains that university and TAFE students on placement need a check but are treated as employees of their institution, which completes the employer steps.

**Contractors and labor hire:** an individual supplied by a personnel provider may work in a risk assessed role only if the registered provider has identified the role to the personnel provider, entered an appropriate contract, and taken reasonable steps to satisfy itself that the individual has a clearance.

blocks.text: The exception ends quickly if conditions slip. Under section 15(2), a person is not in the process of obtaining a clearance on any day an interim bar is in force, at any time they are not supervised as required, or at any time the risk management plan is not being implemented. Section 12 requires that plan to identify each risk to people with disability and explain how it will be managed, and it must be reviewed if the Commissioner requires it or if there is a reportable incident involving a worker. That link to incidents is why screening exceptions belong in the same governance view as [incident management and reportable incidents](/regulations/ndis-incident-management-and-reportable-incidents-training).

sections.heading: What worker screening records must a registered provider keep?

blocks.text: Three sets of records, all kept for 7 years from the date each record is made (section 21). The rules are specific enough that a provider can build a register template directly from them.

items: **Role list (section 17):** a written list of all risk assessed roles, showing the role title or identifier, which paragraph of the definition applies, a description of the role, the date it was assessed, and the name and title of the person who assessed it. The list must be updated within 20 business days of a new risk assessed role being identified or an existing role being reclassified.

**Worker list (section 18):** each worker in a risk assessed role with full name, date of birth, address and role. Cleared workers need the application number, check number, outcome and expiry date, and any suspension or revocation decision. Workers relying on an exception need the exception, its start and end dates, and the supervisor's name. Copies of records about any interim bar, suspension, exclusion or misconduct allegation, and the action taken, must also be kept.

**Personnel records (section 19):** copies of each appropriate contract with a personnel provider, records of administering and enforcing it, information received about each individual, the reasonable steps taken to check their clearance, and any misconduct allegation.

blocks.text: Section 20 sets the form test: the worker list must let an auditor determine which workers were engaged in risk assessed roles on any given day in the seven years before the audit. The NDIS Commission adds that records must survive a worker being unlinked in the portal and be organized, accessible and legible. A list that only shows current staff fails this test, which is a common gap in [audit ready training records](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How long does a clearance last and how is it monitored?

blocks.text: An NDIS Worker Screening Check is valid for up to 5 years from issue unless it is cancelled or revoked. A worker can apply to renew up to 90 days before expiry, applies in the state or territory where they currently live, and does not need to reapply on moving interstate or when a business changes structure, because checks are nationally recognized ([NDIS worker screening](https://www.ndiscommission.gov.au/workforce/worker-screening)).

Monitoring is continuous rather than five yearly. Workers holding a valid clearance are subject to ongoing monitoring, and a linked worker's status in the database can show Clearance, Pending, Interim bar, Exclusion, Suspension or No valid clearance. Employers receive a notification when a linked worker's check is about to expire. A provider confirms a current clearance by checking that the status is Clearance, the expiry date is in the future and the worker is shown as eligible to work.

blocks.title: Portal change on October 12, 2026
blocks.text: From October 12, 2026, registered and deregistered providers do worker screening in the new NDIS Commission Portal, including database access, verification requests and linking or unlinking workers. Unregistered providers, self-managed participants and government agencies keep using their existing portals, and the NDIS Worker Screening Database itself is not moving. Providers should check that their screening procedures and staff instructions name the correct portal.

sections.heading: Do unregistered NDIS providers need worker screening?

blocks.text: Not by law. The NDIS Commission states that unregistered providers are not legally required to ask staff to hold an NDIS worker screening clearance, but it recommends that they make sure all workers have one, and self-managed and plan-managed participants can decide whether their workers must be screened ([unregistered providers](https://www.ndiscommission.gov.au/workforce/worker-screening/worker-screening-unregistered-providers)). Workers pay a fee for the check, so the Commission asks providers to give out their Employer ID only when they genuinely intend to engage the worker.

Clearances also travel into other schemes. The [Aged Care Act 2024 worker obligations](/regulations/aged-care-act-2024-worker-obligations) accept an NDIS clearance for aged care worker screening, and Victoria's voluntary disability worker registration lets applicants quote an NDIS Worker Screening ID instead of a new police check (see [Victorian disability worker registration](/regulations/victoria-disability-worker-registration-and-standards)). Child-related roles may also need a state check, covered in [Working with Children Check requirements](/regulations/working-with-children-check-requirements). For a sector view, see [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats each risk assessed role as a defined object that links the screening requirement, the training obligations and the evidence for that role. When a role is reclassified, the affected people, records and training can be seen together, which supports the 20 business day update and the day by day reconstruction an auditor can ask for.

faqs.q: Does a back office worker at a registered NDIS provider need a clearance?
faqs.a: Usually not, unless the role is key personnel, delivers specified supports or services, or is likely to require more than incidental contact with people with disability. The rules' own example is an accountant who only exchanges polite greetings with customers. The provider must still assess the role, and record the outcome if it is risk assessed.

faqs.q: Can a new worker start before their NDIS clearance comes through?
faqs.a: Only if the state or territory where they work allows it, they have submitted a complete application that the provider has verified, they are supervised by someone with a clearance, and the provider is implementing a written risk management plan. The exception stops applying immediately if an interim bar is issued or supervision lapses.

faqs.q: How long must NDIS worker screening records be kept?
faqs.a: Seven years from the date each record is made, under section 21 of the Worker Screening Rules. The worker list must also be kept in a form that lets an auditor work out who was in a risk assessed role on any given day in the previous seven years, so historical entries cannot be overwritten.

faqs.q: Are volunteers covered by NDIS worker screening?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are in a risk assessed role. The NDIS Commission states that people in risk assessed roles can be staff members, volunteers or students doing work experience or placements. A registered provider must treat a volunteer role exactly like a paid role when assessing it and recording clearances.

faqs.q: Does an NDIS clearance need to be renewed every year?
faqs.a: No. A clearance is valid for up to 5 years unless cancelled or revoked, and renewal can start 90 days before expiry. Between renewals the worker is subject to ongoing monitoring, so providers should check database status periodically rather than relying only on the expiry date.

factCheck.claim: Worker Screening Rules s 5: risk assessed role means a key personnel role, a role whose normal duties include direct delivery of specified supports or services, or a role likely to require more than incidental contact; s 6 defines contact and the three indicators of more than incidental contact; latest compilation dated 31 July 2021.

Worker Screening Rules s 13 restricts risk assessed roles to workers with clearance; s 14 exceptions (in process with supervision, risk management plan and jurisdiction allows; secondary school work experience with direct supervision); s 14A no card no start; s 15(2) circumstances ending the in-process exception.
Worker Screening Rules s 12 risk management plan must identify risks and explain management, reviewed if Commissioner requires or a reportable incident involves a worker.

Worker Screening Rules s 17 role list contents and update within 20 business days; s 18 worker list contents; s 19 personnel records; s 20 auditor must be able to determine workers on any given day in prior seven years; s 21 records kept 7 years; Part 3 made under s 73Q, breach is a civil penalty provision.

Key personnel include CEO, directors listed in ASIC, executive staff, managers or board members; people in risk assessed roles can be staff, volunteers or students; higher education students are treated as employees of their institution; records must survive unlinking and be organised, accessible and legible.
From 12 October 2026 registered and deregistered providers do worker screening in the new NDIS Commission Portal; unregistered providers keep existing portals; the database is not moving.
A check is valid for up to 5 years unless cancelled or revoked; renewal can be applied for up to 90 days before expiry; checks are nationally recognised; employers are notified of expiring checks.

Unregistered providers are not legally required to require clearances but the Commission recommends it; status values Clearance, Pending, Interim bar, Exclusion, Suspension, No valid clearance; workers pay a fee; ongoing monitoring.
